topic: Rust (Axum) vs Go (Fiber) vs ASP.NET (.NET JIT + AOT lanes) — Microservice Benchmark v2
overall_framing: Among completed lanes, Go Fiber leads throughput and most tail metrics. Rust Axum trails on RPS but remains competitive and stable. .NET JIT is behind Go on both throughput and tail latency in this run window. .NET AOT is pending due to container/runtime execution blockers, so no final .NET-vs-.NET verdict yet.

interim_category_winners.evidence: c=200 read RPS: Go 12,327.61 vs .NET JIT 9,520.04 vs Rust 5,970.25
k6 tail p99: Go 511.99 ms vs Rust 773.22 ms vs .NET JIT 915.77 ms
k6 pool recovery p99: Go 94.81 ms vs .NET JIT 111.61 ms vs Rust 137.03 ms
write RPS c=50: Go 4,510.48 vs .NET JIT 4,191.38 vs Rust 3,789.22

dotnet_aot_status.reason: AOT lane executed in containerized mode but did not yield a stable completed benchmark artifact in this environment.
blocking_signals: service health probe failures during lane orchestration
cross-engine host networking mismatch during load phase
runtime dependency warning observed in AOT container logs

allowed: Go leads completed-lane throughput and p99 tail in this run window.
Rust shows lower throughput than Go here and competitive tail behavior vs .NET JIT on p99.9.
.NET JIT trails Go in throughput and tail metrics in this benchmark window.
.NET AOT remains unscored in this publish cut due to environment/runtime blockers.
disallowed: Any final claim that compares .NET JIT and .NET AOT as if both are complete.
Any universal claim such as 'X is always faster'.

confidence_notes: Completed-lane metrics come from a consistent run-id window and aggregate v2 artifact. Confidence is reduced only because the planned AOT lane is not complete yet.
caveats: Numbers are from this machine/environment and should be interpreted as within-run comparisons.
wrk summaries currently have null p99 extraction in the aggregate, so tail claims should rely primarily on k6 for this cut.
Final four-lane verdict is pending dotnet-aot completion.
